squirrel.services.storage.database.PostgresService

class squirrel.services.storage.database.PostgresService.PostgresService(connection_string=None, autoconnect=True)[source]

Bases: IDatabaseService

Concrete database service for PostgreSQL via psycopg (v3).

The service supports two calling conventions for mutating operations:

Examples

# Raw SQL
db.insert({"sql": "INSERT INTO t (a) VALUES (%(a)s)", "params": {"a": 1}})

# Structured dict
db.insert({"table": "t", "values": {"a": 1}})
db.insert({"table": "t", "a": 1})  # flat shorthand

All public methods handle rollback on failure and log exceptions via loguru. Connection loss is retried up to _RETRY_ATTEMPTS times with a short back-off before re-raising.

Parameters:

  • connection_string (Optional[str]) – Optional connection string or DSN. If omitted, the environment variables DATABASE_URL or POSTGRES_DSN are consulted.

  • autoconnect (bool) – If True, attempts to connect during initialisation.

execute(statement, params=None, fetch=False)[source]

Execute a statement inside a cursor and optionally return rows.

Parameters:

  • statement (Any) – A psycopg.sql composable or plain SQL string.

  • params (Optional[dict]) – Optional mapping of named parameters for the statement (%(name)s style).

  • fetch (bool) – When True, fetches all rows and includes rows and columns in the returned mapping. When False, the transaction is committed and only rowcount is returned.

Returns:

Result mapping containing success, rowcount and optionally rows and columns.

Return type:

dict

Raises:

psycopg.Error – On database errors; the connection is rolled back before the exception is re-raised.

query(query, params=None, fetch=None)[source]

Execute a SQL query.

insert(data)[source]

Insert a row using either raw SQL or a structured dict.

Parameters:

data (dict) – Either {"sql": "...", "params": {...}} or {"table": "name", "values": {...}} or a flat mapping.

Any

execute_many(statement, params_seq)[source]

Execute statement for each parameter mapping in params_seq.

All executions share a single transaction; any failure triggers a full rollback.

Parameters:

  • statement (str) – Parameterised SQL string (%(col)s placeholders).

  • params_seq (list[dict]) – List of parameter dictionaries, one per execution.

Returns:

True if all executions succeeded, False otherwise.

bool
